admissionSummary.reason:
72-year-old female admitted with community-acquired pneumonia, now hospital day 5 with PICC line for IV antibiotics, right lower lobe consolidation improving on imaging, small right parapneumonic effusion, weaned to room air, tolerating oral intake, ambulating with physical therapy
• Community-acquired pneumonia — day 5, right lower lobe consolidation slightly improved on CXR, small right parapneumonic effusion on CT (non-loculated), on ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily and azithromycin 500 mg daily
• PICC line — placed for IV antibiotics, site clean without redness or tenderness this morning
• Oxygenation — weaned to room air yesterday afternoon, comfortable without supplemental oxygen
• Labs — WBC 11.2, Hgb 10.9, Plt 312, Na 136, K 3.8, Cl 101, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.07, glucose 141, Mg 1.9, PO4 3.3
• Renal ultrasound — no hydronephrosis
• Disposition planning — patient asking about discharge; infectious disease consultation pending regarding PICC line removal; repeat echocardiogram planned for Friday

value.preRoundNotes: Pre-round review for today, written from the morning list before rounds. Hospital day 5 for community-acquired pneumonia, now with a PICC line for IV antibiotics. Overnight quiet, no new complaints, slept well. Labs this morning: WBC 11.2, hemoglobin 10.9, platelets 312, sodium 136, potassium 3.8, chloride 101, bicarbonate 24, BUN 18, creatinine 1.07, glucose 141, magnesium 1.9, phosphorus 3.3. Chest X-ray shows the right lower lobe consolidation slightly improved. CT chest from Tuesday showed a small right parapneumonic effusion, not loculated. Renal ultrasound shows no hydronephrosis. Medications: ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily, azithromycin 500 mg daily, enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneous daily, pantoprazole 40 mg daily, metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, and acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours as needed. She is walking in the hall with physical therapy twice a day and eating most of her meals without nausea. Her daughter visited yesterday evening and asked about the expected length of stay and whether she will need home oxygen. Oxygen was weaned to room air yesterday afternoon and she has stayed comfortable since. The PICC site was clean this morning with no redness or tenderness. She asked again about going home, and we went over the remaining steps in plain terms. Continue the current antibiotics for now and reassess the total course length with pharmacy. Plan: ask infectious disease about removing the PICC line, and book a repeat echocardiogram for Friday.
